gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on September 4?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 4 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent official forecasts from sources including the German Weather Service and global models indicate mostly clear skies and light westerly winds over Munich on September 4, supporting daytime maximum temperatures in the upper 20s °C under stable high-pressure conditions. These conditions favor strong solar heating with minimal cloud interference or precipitation, aligning with the market’s strong implied probability for a 29–30 °C high. Historical September 4 records show a 30.9 °C peak, while recent years have reached 28–29 °C, providing context for trader positioning. Updated model consensus and the absence of cooling fronts in the latest runs reinforce expectations near these thresholds ahead of final observations.

These conditions align with seasonal averages around 21°C while suppressing any spike above 23°C, explaining the market's heavy weighting toward 22°C at 52.5% implied probability. Westerly winds advect milder Atlantic air, and recent model runs have converged on modest afternoon peaks without significant clearing. Traders monitor updated Met Office observations and any late-day breaks in cloud cover that could nudge readings toward 23°C, though current guidance keeps higher outcomes below 5% odds.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 4 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Current forecast consensus from Met Office, GFS, and other models indicates a peak temperature of 21–22°C in London on September 4, 2026, driven by persistent cloud cover, light rain or drizzle in the morning, and moderate westerly winds that limit daytime heating.** 

These conditions follow a mild start to the month with typical early-autumn Atlantic airflow suppressing any strong warming. Afternoon clearing may allow brief rises toward 22–23°C in some areas, but overall model agreement keeps extremes unlikely. This scientific outlook—rooted in observed pressure patterns around 1013–1016 hPa and dew points supporting modest humidity—explains why traders have concentrated implied probability on the 21–23°C outcomes, with 22°C leading at 54%. Minor forecast revisions from new model runs could still shift the exact maximum before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Persistent rain and extensive cloud cover from a northeast-flowing system are capping daytime heating in Tokyo, keeping forecast highs clustered in the mid-20s Celsius for September 5.** Official guidance from the Japan Meteorological Agency and global models (including GFS and ECMWF runs) indicate overcast skies with light to moderate precipitation and northeasterly winds of 7–12 mph, which limit solar insolation and promote evaporative cooling. This setup produces a tight distribution around 25–26°C peaks, with hourly profiles showing afternoon maxima rarely exceeding 27°C amid high humidity (70–90%) and stable pressure near 1013–1014 hPa. Minor model differences in exact cloud timing and wind strength create the near-even split between 25°C and 26°C implied probabilities, while historical September averages near 29°C highlight how this transient pattern deviates from climatology. Fresh model updates overnight and morning observations will refine the final peak.

Surface high pressure and northerly advection of drier air are suppressing widespread cloud cover and allowing strong solar heating, yet the modest humidity and light flow keep the peak from climbing higher. The tight 40.5 %–37.5 % split between the 84–85 °F and 86–87 °F bins reflects lingering uncertainty in the precise timing of any clearing versus scattered cumulus that could shave a degree or two off the maximum. Historical climatology places the September 4 average at 80 °F, so current conditions remain modestly above normal but well below record territory.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest Japan Meteorological Agency guidance and ensemble forecasts point to a high of 25–26 °C in Tokyo on September 5 under persistent cloud cover and scattered rain. Northeasterly flow advects cooler, moist marine air while extensive stratiform clouds sharply reduce surface insolation, limiting afternoon warming. This pattern follows several days of similar conditions that have already depressed daytime maxima several degrees below September climatology. Model spread remains modest, with most runs clustering between 24–27 °C; the precise peak hinges on any brief afternoon clearing and exact rainfall timing. Traders therefore assign nearly equal weight to the two leading bins, reflecting the narrow but genuine forecast uncertainty around these thresholds.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 4 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Trader consensus reflected in the market-implied odds places the strongest probability on 24°C, with secondary support for 23°C and 25°C, consistent with typical model spread and uncertainty in exact rainfall timing and intensity. Updated model runs and official briefings from agencies like DWD will provide the next key data points ahead of resolution.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Trader consensus reflected in the 45.5% implied probability for 24°C aligns with this guidance, with smaller probabilities assigned to 25°C and 23°C capturing remaining model spread and uncertainty in exact timing of cloud cover. Final resolution will depend on official observations from Munich stations, with no major forecast shifts reported in the past 24 hours.

gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on September 6?

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 6 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from multiple models, including Met Office, ECMWF-influenced sources, and high-resolution guidance, converge on a daytime high of 23–24°C for Munich on September 6 under clear to mostly clear skies and light northeasterly winds. This reflects a post-frontal high-pressure regime drawing cooler continental air after warmer conditions earlier in the week. The September 6 climatological average high stands at 21.2°C, so current guidance sits modestly above normal but without strong warm advection or subsidence that would support 25°C or higher. Model consensus has remained stable in the latest runs, with minimal spread and low precipitation risk, supporting the market’s heavy weighting toward 23–24°C outcomes as the most probable range.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from agencies and meteorological services indicate a high of 23–24°C in Munich on September 5, driven by a westerly flow advecting cooler maritime air and widespread rain that limits daytime heating. Multiple runs, including GFS guidance, show afternoon temperatures peaking near 23°C amid light to moderate precipitation and high cloud cover, consistent with the market’s heaviest weighting on 24°C (45.5%) followed by 25°C (23.5%) and 23°C (21%). Historical September averages near 21°C provide context, while the current setup’s steering pattern and moisture reduce upside potential for 26°C or higher. Traders appear to be incorporating the latest model consensus and typical forecast uncertainty ranges, with resolution depending on the precise timing and intensity of showers.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from multiple models, including Met Office, ECMWF-influenced sources, and high-resolution guidance, converge on a daytime high of 23–24°C for Munich on September 6 under clear to mostly clear skies and light northeasterly winds. This reflects a post-frontal high-pressure regime drawing cooler continental air after warmer conditions earlier in the week. The September 6 climatological average high stands at 21.2°C, so current guidance sits modestly above normal but without strong warm advection or subsidence that would support 25°C or higher. Model consensus has remained stable in the latest runs, with minimal spread and low precipitation risk, supporting the market’s heavy weighting toward 23–24°C outcomes as the most probable range.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecast model consensus from sources including the GFS and European models indicates a high of 23–24°C in Munich on September 5, driven by a passing cold front that follows unusually warm conditions on September 4. This system is expected to deliver widespread cloud cover, scattered showers or thunderstorms, and a shift to westerly winds, suppressing daytime heating relative to the long-term September average high of 21.4°C. Market-implied odds concentrate on 24°C as the modal outcome because current guidance shows limited warming potential once precipitation begins, though minor model spreads around timing and intensity keep 23°C and 25°C in play. Traders appear to weigh the cooling influence of cloud cover and moisture against any brief clearing that could allow slightly higher readings before resolution.

gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in London on September 4?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 4 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Updated model runs and official observations closer to the date will refine the exact maximum.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 6 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent European and global forecast models indicate a high-pressure ridge building over central Europe after a frontal passage on September 5, favoring mostly clear skies and light northeasterly winds for Munich on September 6. This setup supports maximum temperatures clustering around 23–24 °C, consistent with the market’s leading implied probabilities and slightly above the 1991–2020 climatological average high of 21.2 °C. Model agreement remains high with limited spread, though minor revisions in boundary-layer moisture or timing of any residual cloud could shift the peak by 1 °C. Updated runs from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts and National Weather Service equivalents over the next 48 hours will provide the next key data points for traders.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on the London highest temperature market for September 4, 2026, centers on 22°C due to Met Office forecasts showing a maximum of 22–23°C amid morning rain clearing to overcast skies with blustery westerly winds. Current observations place daytime readings near 20–21°C under persistent cloud cover, consistent with early September climatology where typical highs range 18–22°C. Model guidance indicates limited diurnal warming potential from Atlantic airflow and residual moisture, reducing odds of exceeding 23°C. The 86% implied probability for 22°C aligns with official maximum temperature projections, while lower probabilities for 24°C+ reflect the absence of southerly flow or clear-sky amplification needed for higher readings. Updated agency briefings through the afternoon will refine final resolution.

gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in London on September 5?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Minimal cloud cover and dry air favor efficient solar heating without significant moisture or frontal activity to suppress maxima, while the brief cool-down after September 5 thunderstorms limits upside potential. Updated model runs through early September 4 show little divergence, keeping 22–25°C outcomes dominant ahead of final observations.

gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in London on September 4?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 4 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Forecast models and real-time observations position 30°C as the leading outcome for Munich’s daily maximum on September 4, 2026.** Clear to partly cloudy skies, light-to-moderate southwesterly flow shifting westerly, and strong insolation under a stable late-summer high-pressure ridge have allowed temperatures to climb steadily through the afternoon, with hourly readings approaching or reaching 30°C at multiple urban stations. This aligns with the historical daily record of 30.9°C set in 1929 and exceeds recent September 4 values (28.6°C in 2024). Trader consensus at 63% for 30°C and 22.5% for 31°C reflects the narrow window between model consensus near 29–30°C and the possibility of brief additional warming before evening cooling. Official resolution will depend on the highest verified reading from the primary Munich station network, with no major synoptic changes expected before sunset.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent cloud cover, widespread rain, and northeasterly winds are limiting daytime heating and keeping the September 5 high temperature in Tokyo closely contested between 25°C and 26°C. Official guidance shows overcast conditions with 70–100% cloud cover through the afternoon, light to moderate precipitation, and steady northeast flow of cooler marine air that reduces solar insolation and caps warming. Model consensus places peak readings near 24–27°C, with 26°C slightly favored in some runs due to brief afternoon breaks in the clouds. This pattern deviates from the late-summer climatological average near 29°C, reflecting the influence of an active frontal system. Market-implied odds align with this narrow range and the inherent uncertainty in exact peak timing and cloud breaks before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Official Japan Meteorological Agency observations and short-range model guidance show Tokyo’s maximum temperature on September 4 reached 27 °C amid widespread rain and persistent cloud cover that limited daytime heating.**  

Surface data from the Tokyo station recorded a peak near this value under northeasterly flow and high humidity, consistent with ensemble forecasts that suppressed readings above the seasonal normal of roughly 29 °C. With the date nearly concluded and no late-day warming expected, trader consensus has converged on this outcome. Only an extreme measurement revision or localized microclimate anomaly could shift the result, both of which carry negligible probability given the dense observational network.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 6 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service forecasts and ensemble model consensus indicate a mostly sunny Sunday with northeasterly flow at 5–10 mph advecting cooler maritime air into the New York metro area, supporting a daily maximum in the mid-70s. This pattern, established after a frontal passage earlier in the week, deviates below the 1991–2020 climatological average high of 79.5°F. Differentiation between 74–75°F and 76–77°F outcomes hinges on subtle variations in boundary-layer mixing, exact cloud cover during peak heating hours, and minor shifts in the position of a weak surface ridge; official point forecasts cluster near 74–75°F at Central Park and LaGuardia. Limited precipitation chances (around 20%) and stable dew points in the upper 50s to low 60s further constrain upward temperature excursions, though latest model runs could adjust the final observed high before resolution.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Official Japan Meteorological Agency observations and short-range model guidance show Tokyo’s maximum temperature on September 4 reached 27 °C amid widespread rain and persistent cloud cover that limited daytime heating.**  

Surface data from the Tokyo station recorded a peak near this value under northeasterly flow and high humidity, consistent with ensemble forecasts that suppressed readings above the seasonal normal of roughly 29 °C. With the date nearly concluded and no late-day warming expected, trader consensus has converged on this outcome. Only an extreme measurement revision or localized microclimate anomaly could shift the result, both of which carry negligible probability given the dense observational network.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 6 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the LaGuardia Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 4 Sep '26.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service forecasts and ensemble model consensus indicate a mostly sunny Sunday with northeasterly flow at 5–10 mph advecting cooler maritime air into the New York metro area, supporting a daily maximum in the mid-70s. This pattern, established after a frontal passage earlier in the week, deviates below the 1991–2020 climatological average high of 79.5°F. Differentiation between 74–75°F and 76–77°F outcomes hinges on subtle variations in boundary-layer mixing, exact cloud cover during peak heating hours, and minor shifts in the position of a weak surface ridge; official point forecasts cluster near 74–75°F at Central Park and LaGuardia. Limited precipitation chances (around 20%) and stable dew points in the upper 50s to low 60s further constrain upward temperature excursions, though latest model runs could adjust the final observed high before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: **National Weather Service forecasts and real-time observations position mid-80s temperatures as the dominant outcome for New York City’s September 4 high.** Models and agency products from the New York forecast office converge on highs of 84–86 °F at key stations including Central Park, LaGuardia, and JFK, driven by northwest flow, partly sunny skies, and only limited shower activity that has not substantially cooled the boundary layer. These values sit modestly above the 1991–2020 average high of 80 °F for the date, reflecting residual warmth after an 88 °F reading on September 3. With the daily maximum typically recorded in the afternoon and official verification drawn from airport and Central Park thermometers, the tight clustering of 84–87 °F bins captures the current consensus range while leaving modest room for slight upward or downward revisions as final observations are tallied.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official forecasts from the National Weather Service and ensemble models indicate a high in the upper 70s to low 80s for New York City on September 5, driven by a northerly wind shift delivering drier, cooler air after recent humid conditions with highs near 84°F. gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in NYC on September 6?

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecasts from the National Weather Service and regional models indicate a highest temperature in the mid-80s for New York City today, driven by northwest winds advecting cooler air behind a frontal passage and partly sunny skies with limited afternoon heating. This positions the 84-85°F bin as the market leader at 55% implied probability, followed by 86-87°F at 31%, consistent with ensemble consensus around 84–86°F and well above the 1991–2020 average high of 80°F for September 4. Scattered showers and thunderstorms possible this afternoon introduce modest uncertainty in peak readings, while historical records show 90°F+ extremes are rare this late in the season without strong high-pressure ridging. Official observations from Central Park or LaGuardia will determine resolution by day’s end.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Recent model runs show minimal disagreement, with afternoon peaks held below seasonal normals by widespread overcast conditions and light rain. Traders have priced 26°C highest (40.5%) and 25°C next (34.5%), reflecting the narrow but well-defined range between official guidance and ensemble outputs. Resolution will hinge on the precise peak observed by the Japan Meteorological Agency’s Tokyo station amid these stable synoptic conditions.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent cloud cover, widespread rain, and northerly winds are suppressing daytime heating across the Tokyo region ahead of September 6, keeping official forecast highs clustered between 23–25 °C according to multiple numerical models. The dominant low-pressure system and associated frontal activity limit solar insolation and enhance evaporative cooling, preventing the higher temperatures typical for early September. Market-implied odds favor 24 °C (34 %) and 25 °C (30.5 %) because small differences in the timing and intensity of heaviest rainfall or wind gusts can shift the daily maximum by 1 °C. Traders weigh the consensus of global and regional models against the narrow uncertainty range created by variable cloud breaks or slight steering-pattern shifts before resolution.
